comparator.name: Dutch Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden study product assigns 60 EC to each of three years and describes intensive Dutch acquisition alongside Dutch linguistics, literature, history, art and society. Its listed unique components support 60 EC in year one, 55 additional EC in year two and 60 EC in year three. The same 5-EC module, Core Curriculum: Humanities in a Digital World (5000VHDW2Y), appears in both the Year 1 and Year 2 compulsory groups; a student cannot earn the same module twice. The 2026–27 programme-specific OER confirms that the programme changed from 1 September 2026 and contains first-year transitional provisions, but it does not identify a distinct 5-EC replacement that would make the displayed three-year curriculum a coherent 180-EC pathway. The current year-three structure is represented with the 10-EC compulsory language-acquisition component, the first two listed 5-EC linguistics-oriented choices, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC elective space. The OER states that formal specialisations are not applicable, so routeSelection is null.

exception.reason: The current 2026–27 study product lists Core Curriculum: Humanities in a Digital World (module 5000VHDW2Y, 5 EC) as compulsory in both year one and year two. Counting that identical module twice would falsely satisfy the 180-EC requirement. The programme-specific OER confirms a curriculum change from September 2026 but does not establish which distinct 5-EC component replaces the duplicated second-year entry. A complete coherent comparator pathway therefore cannot be certified from the current official sources.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported unique curriculum totals 175 EC: 60 EC in year one, 55 additional unique EC in year two after counting Humanities in a Digital World only once, and 60 EC in year three comprising 10 EC advanced Dutch language acquisition, 10 EC instantiated linguistics-oriented choice, a 10-EC BA thesis and 30 EC open elective space. The programme’s defining Dutch-language progression and Dutch culture, history, literature and linguistics remain clear, but no-defensible-match evaluation requires a complete 180-EC comparator. Revisit the UCR-match decision once Leiden identifies the missing distinct 5-EC component or corrects the duplicate.
